notes: The experiment manipulates gelsemine as nectar defence and measures both nectar robbers and pollinators. Total pollinator visits are numerically recovered for both years; 2004 is the natural-range primary effect. Residence/proportion probed and pollen analogue remain separate outcomes.

Publisher abstract explicitly identifies defensive chemicals in floral nectar and context-dependent pollinator deterrence. Full numerical contrasts are still required; alternative-flower context must remain a moderator/stratum.

The source shows nectar repellents reduce ant visitation and alter pollinator use, while nicotine is an efficient herbivore defence. However, visit number and residence/removal move in different directions, and the exact nicotine-to-antagonist link must be kept distinct before primary B pooling.
Field effect occurs only at strongly elevated concentrations; natural/near-natural treatment produced no detected visitation or reproduction cost.
Potentially valuable because the same study explicitly includes mutualist bees and antagonist butterflies; audit for direct B-to-P and B-to-H effects and dependence.
Useful only if the focal compound independently satisfies the flower-specific antagonist-reduction role; preserve microbe interaction.

Strong strict-B source: Aconitum nectar alkaloids deter robbers at lower concentrations and pollinator visitation declines with alkaloid concentration. The field B-to-P relationship is observational rather than a treatment/control manipulation, so it is not pooled with Adler's manipulation lnRR. Raw Figshare data remain the preferred route for exact effect reconstruction.

Numerical preference effects are recovered from source-reported t and df, but the focal experiment does not itself establish a flower-specific antagonist-reduction role for nicotine. It remains outside the primary strict-B pool.
